es: Rebatir con tacto y firmeza usando atenuantes, refuerzos y frases hendidas en un texto argumentativo.

teaching.en: What matters is the cost of the new benches, and it is the cost that many families overlook.
teaching.es: Lo que importa es el coste de los bancos nuevos, y es el coste lo que muchas familias pasan por alto.
teaching.explanationEs: Frase hendida con What…is y con It is…that: las dos colocan el coste en primer plano.
segments: What matters is the cost of the new benches,
and it is the cost that many families overlook.
teaching.audioText: What matters is the cost of the new benches, and it is the cost that many families overlook.

teaching.en: The plan is arguably the cheapest option, but it is by no means the fairest for families with three children.
teaching.es: El plan es posiblemente la opción más barata, pero de ningún modo es la más justa para las familias con tres hijos.
teaching.explanationEs: Arguably atenúa (no puedes probarlo); by no means refuerza la negación. Son dos matices distintos.
segments: The plan is arguably the cheapest option, but it is
by no means the fairest for families with three children.
teaching.audioText: The plan is arguably the cheapest option, but it is by no means the fairest for families with three children.

teaching.en: That is a reasonable point, yet I have reservations about the timing, which could hardly be worse for shopkeepers.
teaching.es: Es un punto razonable, pero tengo reservas sobre el momento elegido, que no podría ser peor para los comerciantes.
teaching.explanationEs: Concede (reasonable point) y rebate con tacto: have reservations about suaviza un desacuerdo real.
segments: That is a reasonable point, yet I have reservations about
the timing, which could hardly be worse for shopkeepers.
teaching.audioText: That is a reasonable point, yet I have reservations about the timing, which could hardly be worse for shopkeepers.

teaching.en: The fee is undoubtedly a problem for large families, and far from easing the burden, the plan would increase it.
teaching.es: La cuota es sin duda un problema para las familias numerosas y, lejos de aliviar la carga, el plan la aumentaría.
teaching.explanationEs: Undoubtedly refuerza lo que sí sostienes; far from + -ing equivale a «lejos de» y introduce lo contrario de lo esperado.
segments: The fee is undoubtedly a problem for large families, and
far from easing the burden, the plan would increase it.
teaching.audioText: The fee is undoubtedly a problem for large families, and far from easing the burden, the plan would increase it.

teaching.en: To a large degree the dispute is about trust, and what is essential is a fair price for every family.
teaching.es: En gran medida la disputa trata de la confianza, y lo esencial es un precio justo para cada familia.
teaching.explanationEs: To a large degree es un atenuante de cantidad; What is essential is… es otra frase hendida con What.
segments: To a large degree the dispute is about trust, and
what is essential is a fair price for every family.
teaching.audioText: To a large degree the dispute is about trust, and what is essential is a fair price for every family.

teaching.en: Councillors who oppose the plan should drive the point home calmly, because a raised voice rarely wins a neighbourhood debate.
teaching.es: Los concejales que se oponen al plan deberían dejarlo bien claro con calma, porque levantar la voz rara vez gana un debate vecinal.
teaching.explanationEs: Drive the point home = dejar algo bien claro; el tono sereno también es un recurso de firmeza.

prompt.es: Elige la frase hendida que destaca «el tráfico» como lo que molesta a los vecinos.

choices.text: It is the traffic that bothers most of the neighbours.
The traffic is bothering most of the neighbours.
It is the traffic what bothers most of the neighbours.

feedback.es: La hendida con It is + elemento + that pone el tráfico en primer plano; tras el elemento destacado no se usa what.

hint.es: Busca It is + lo destacado + that + verbo.

prompt.es: Completa: «El plan es posiblemente la opción más barata, aunque no puedo demostrarlo.»

feedback.es: Arguably atenúa una afirmación que no puedes probar; undoubtedly la reforzaría y contradiría «I cannot prove it».

hint.es: Adverbio de cautela; empieza por a.

origin.text: The council's figures are still incomplete. The plan is ___ the cheapest option, although I cannot prove it.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Lo que importa a los vecinos es el ruido por la noche.»

answer.text: What matters to the neighbours is the noise at night
accepted: What matters to the neighbours is the noise at night
The noise at night is what matters to the neighbours

feedback.es: What + sujeto + verbo + is + X: la hendida con What coloca el ruido por la noche como lo destacado.

hint.es: Empieza por What matters y cierra con is + lo importante.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige la postura de la hablante ante el plan.

choices.text: She is convinced the plan is flawed and wants the vote cancelled.
She backs the plan cautiously and wants the figures published.
She accepts the plan as it stands and sees no need for more information.

feedback.es: La hablante tiene reservas, pero considera el plan «arguably the best we have» y pide ver las cifras antes de votar: apoyo cauteloso, ni rechazo ni confianza total.

origin.audio: Councillors are undoubtedly under pressure, and I have reservations about the timing. The plan is by no means perfect, but it is arguably the best we have. What matters now is that residents can see the figures before they vote.

prompt.es: ¿Qué afirma el autor sin ninguna reserva en este fragmento?

choices.text: That the lane has reduced the number of accidents.
That the lane may eventually save the council some money.
That the new cycle lane is popular among local people.
That the road now feels safer to every cyclist.

feedback.es: Undoubtedly refuerza la popularidad del carril; las demás afirmaciones van atenuadas (harder to prove, arguably, may, nobody can say).

origin.text: Our new cycle lane is undoubtedly popular, but the claim that it has cut accidents is harder to prove. It has arguably made the road feel safer, and far from being a waste of money, it may even save some, although nobody can say by how much.

prompt.es: Reformula con una frase hendida que empiece por What.

answer.text: What worries the residents is the price.
accepted: What worries the residents is the price.
What concerns the residents is the price.
What bothers the residents is the price.
What troubles the residents is the price.

feedback.es: What + verbo + sujeto + is + X convierte the price en lo destacado de la frase.

prompt.es: Escucha el fragmento y elige cómo se dirige Carlos a Mia al rebatir su propuesta.

choices.text: Firmly, but only about the timing, since he accepts the charge in principle.
Cautiously, agreeing with her while hoping she will drop the proposal.
Emotionally, appealing to the neighbours' anger rather than to the facts.
Politely, acknowledging her point before he goes on to disagree.

feedback.es: Carlos empieza concediendo que Mia tiene un punto razonable y solo después rebate, con tono sereno: cortesía sin perder firmeza; no acepta el cobro en principio ni apela a la ira de los vecinos.

origin.audio: Carlos got up at the residents' meeting to answer Mia's proposal for a parking charge. He began by conceding that she had a reasonable point: the street really is crowded at weekends. Then he chose his words with care. The plan is arguably the simplest option, he said, but it is by no means the fairest, because it is the cost that families with two cars will overlook until the first bill arrives. He added that he had reservations about the timing, since a charge introduced in January would hit people who had just paid for the holidays. He never raised his voice. He simply repeated, calmly, that what matters is that nobody is priced out of their own street.

prompt.es: Escucha de nuevo: ¿qué sugiere Carlos sobre las familias con dos autos?

choices.text: That some households would only discover the burden when the bills arrive.
That families with one car would pay nothing at all.
That Mia has hidden the real cost from the residents on purpose.
That the shops on the street would lose customers because of the charge.

feedback.es: Carlos dice que las familias con dos autos pasarán por alto el coste hasta recibir la primera factura: sugiere un impacto que muchos no anticipan; no acusa a Mia, no habla de comercios ni promete gratuidad a nadie.

prompt.es: Escribe tu intervención: concesión, refutación con frase hendida y cierre.

answer.text: In my view, pupils should clean their own classroom once a week. Admittedly, it takes time away from lessons, and I have reservations about how often we can do it during exams. That is a reasonable point, but what matters is the habit we build: it is the pupils who use the room every day who should look after it, and it is undoubtedly fairer that everyone shares the work. Arguably, a clean room also helps us study, because nobody concentrates well among rubbish. Far from being a burden, ten minutes on Friday is a small price to pay. It is the cost of extra staff that the school would carry otherwise, and that money could buy books instead. To a large degree, the question is about respect, and what is essential is that we treat the classroom as ours. To conclude, a tidy room by no means needs a cleaner, only a rota.
accepted: In my view, pupils should clean their own classroom once a week. Admittedly, it takes time away from lessons, and I have reservations about how often we can do it during exams. That is a reasonable point, but what matters is the habit we build: it is the pupils who use the room every day who should look after it, and it is undoubtedly fairer that everyone shares the work. Arguably, a clean room also helps us study, because nobody concentrates well among rubbish. Far from being a burden, ten minutes on Friday is a small price to pay. It is the cost of extra staff that the school would carry otherwise, and that money could buy books instead. To a large degree, the question is about respect, and what is essential is that we treat the classroom as ours. To conclude, a tidy room by no means needs a cleaner, only a rota.

I believe that pupils should clean their classroom every week. I concede that it takes time from lessons, and some parents think the school should do it. That is a valid point, but what counts is the habit we learn. It is the pupils who use the room all day, so it is undoubtedly fair that we look after it. Arguably, a clean room helps us study, because nobody concentrates well among rubbish. It is also the cost that the school would save, and that money could buy books for the library. Far from being unfair, ten minutes on Friday is a small price to pay. To a large degree this is a question of respect, and what is essential is that we share the work, because the classroom belongs to all of us. In conclusion, the whole class benefits, and nobody is asked to do more than a fair share.

feedback.es: Una buena intervención concede antes de rebatir, usa al menos una frase hendida, equilibra atenuantes y refuerzos y cierra con una conclusión.

origin.text: Debate escolar: ¿deben los alumnos limpiar su aula una vez por semana? Defiendes que sí. Escribe unas 190–250 palabras: concede que se pierde tiempo de clase; rebate con frases hendidas (What matters is…; It is the cost that…); usa un atenuante (arguably) y un refuerzo (undoubtedly); y cierra con una conclusión.

prompt.es: ¿Con qué actitud escribe la remitente esta respuesta al municipio?

choices.text: Apologetic, accepting that residents had read the old rule wrongly.
Polite, but firm that the council's silence was the real problem.
Hostile, blaming the council for writing a confusing rule.
Neutral, merely reporting what other residents have said.

feedback.es: Agradece y concede que la norma era difícil, pero con «That said» desplaza el problema al silencio del municipio: cortesía con firmeza.

origin.text: Dear Councillor, thank you for your reply. You are right that the old rule was hard to follow, and we are grateful for your patience. That said, what worries the residents is not the wording but the silence that followed: it is the lack of any answer that has cost the council their trust.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Es el momento elegido lo que el municipio pasa por alto.»

answer.text: It is the timing that the council overlooks

feedback.es: It is + elemento + that + resto: la hendida coloca the timing como lo destacado.

prompt.es: Completa: «Tengo reservas sobre el momento elegido y quisiera más tiempo para estudiarlo.»

feedback.es: Have reservations about es la fórmula tactful para expresar un desacuerdo moderado; doubts o concerns también encajan.
